title: Food
hookLine: eating with thanks, sharing with the hungry
tomorrow: God finally answers Job. why does he talk about rain on empty land?

cards: Lunch trays, takeout bags, a granola bar eaten at a red light: plenty of meals go by without anyone noticing them. John tells of one that got noticed. A crowd far from town, hungry.

A boy has “five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?” And before anything multiplies, Jesus does one small thing. He gives thanks, for a lunch that is clearly not enough.

teach.h: THANKS FIRST, WHILE IT LOOKS SMALL.
teach.b: That's the order John keeps: “And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed”. Thanks first, while the bread still looks small. Then sharing, until everyone eats.
Today's line holds both halves. The thanks says food is a gift before it's a meal.
The First Letter to Timothy says it plainly: “every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving.”
Christians say grace in different forms: sung, spoken, silent, with the sign of the cross. The sharing says the gift was never for one table only.

teach.h: DEAL THY BREAD TO THE HUNGRY.
teach.b: Isaiah describes the kind of fast God wants: “Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry?” And the first believers in Acts ate together “with gladness and singleness of heart.”
Notice how this week's lines show up at a table. Gentleness and respect, eating with a friend who doesn't pray.
Money as a servant, buying groceries for someone else. Attention guarded, phone face down, so the meal gets noticed. One table can hold the whole week.

how: Christians say grace before meals in different ways, from a sung blessing to a silent sign of the cross; churches run food pantries and shared meals, and some keep fasts that send what's saved to the hungry.

o: a reward earned by a hard day's work
a gift to receive with thanks and pass along
fuel the body needs, and nothing more

games.q: one table, one week — tap the pairs.
p: deal thy bread to the hungry

s: in John, Jesus gives thanks only after the bread multiplies
he gives thanks first, while it's still five loaves and two fishes.
in John, the loaves come from a boy's lunch
a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes.
Isaiah links the fast God wants with feeding the hungry

games.q: you made too much soup. your neighbor just lost her job and won't ask anyone for help. what fits thanks and sharing?
o: bring her a container, simply, the way you'd share with a friend.
freeze it; sharing is what the official food drive is for.
give thanks for your full pantry and leave it there.
games.why: Isaiah: deal thy bread to the hungry. thanks for the gift, then it goes out the door.

practice: Take a bite or a sip of something near you, slowly, and taste it all the way through: the first note, the texture, what stays afterward. Say a quiet thank you, in whatever words are yours.
Then bring to mind one person you could share a meal or a snack with this week.

wordCard.voice: Food. A gift before it's a meal: received with thanks, and passed along to the hungry.

orig.note: Greek: having given thanks. John 6:11; the same verb family as the church word Eucharist.

carryVoice: Your line: thanks and sharing, the two things Jesus did with five loaves. That's the week.
